title: The editor stops closing itself the moment it opens
highlights: Found it: the text box was being closed by a blur that had nothing to do with the user. The field ended its edit on any blur at all — and a freshly focused field blurs on its own when the window loses focus, when the page scrolls, or from the layout shift caused by the field appearing. It opened and closed within a few milliseconds of the press, which is why every report for four releases said “no field” while the field had, in fact, existed

An edit now ends because of something the user did: Escape, a press somewhere else, or focus genuinely moving to another control. A blur to nothing keeps the editor open and puts the caret back, because a field that is open but not focused takes no typing and looks exactly as broken as one that never opened

The diagnostic now watches the field’s whole life rather than sampling it. It reports a field that was rendered and removed separately from one that never appeared — the distinction that took four releases to make — and reports any exception thrown while the press is handled

Two new browser tests cover the halves of this: a stray blur must leave the editor open and focused with typing still working, and a press on the backdrop must still close it. The first fails without the fix

title: The press no longer needs a lookup to find the box it belongs to
highlights: Fixed the reported bug: the press arrived, the handler ran, and no field appeared. The handler found the code that opens the box by looking it up in a map — and when the lookup found nothing, it did nothing, silently, while still counting as handled. That is why every diagnostic for four releases said “the press handler ran” next to “no field”
The handler is now given the code to run instead of looking it up, so the ordinary path cannot fail this way at all. A missing map entry is now harmless rather than silent
The new report line showed it: “+21ms the button handler ran” followed by no field, which ruled out the press never arriving and pointed straight at what the handler did next
New test presses a box the map has never seen and requires it to open. Put the lookup back and the test fails, which is the reported symptom exactly

title: The diagnostic stops guessing, and says when it cannot see
highlights: Fixed the diagnostic itself. The line that reported whether the press handler ran was measured in the browser’s very first listen to the press — before the press had been handed to anything — so it always answered “did not run”. A real report was read as if that meant something. The report is now a timeline: each step is recorded at the moment it happens, and a step is only called missing once the whole gesture is over

The report now answers the question that decides the fix. It can tell whether the press survives as far as the page at all. If it does not, nothing inside the app can ever act on it, and the report says so plainly instead of blaming the text box or the rescue
Three new browser tests hold the diagnostic to this: a working press, a press stopped part-way down, and a press stopped above the page must each produce a different, correct report

title: The diagnostic now says whether the rescue caught the press
highlights: “No field” had two explanations and now has three: the press never reached the button, the press reached it and the edit was discarded, or the rescue was supposed to step in and did not. The report names which of the three happened, so the next report is the last one

Fixed the arrival line itself: it asked whether the pressed element had a marker, and a target that is not an element answered “no” to a question it was never asked, so the report could have blamed an absent handler for a press that was handled

title: Opening a card’s text no longer depends on the press arriving
highlights: The text edit now has a second way in. If a press on a text box is stopped before it reaches the box — by anything between the browser and the page — the sheet notices and opens the field itself, so the box opens either way

The rescue is installed once per sheet, not once per text box. The first version put a listener inside every box: a twelve-card sheet installed twenty-four of them, one press ran all of them, they fought, and no field opened at all — which reproduced the very bug it was meant to cure. A missing wire is now a compile error rather than a box that silently stops opening

The rescue never runs during a press that is already working. It waits for the press to finish and only steps in if the box’s own handler never ran; otherwise the field would open and close within the same gesture, which is exactly what the first version did
New browser test severs both of the button’s own ways in and requires the field to still open, exactly once. With the rescue disabled the test fails, so it tests the rescue and not something else

title: A one-click diagnostic for “the text will not open”
highlights: Added a magnifier button beside the version. Press it, then click a card’s text, and it reports which build is running, which element the browser actually delivered the press to, whether the text box is the height it claims to be, and whether a field opened and kept the caret

The report now answers the question that decides the fix: “no field” means the press never started an edit, while “field present, focus is BODY” means it opened and something took the caret. Those are different bugs with different fixes

Checking every release by rebuilding it and driving a real mouse press confirms 1.7.0 through 1.8.0 work, 1.8.1 does not, and 1.8.2 onwards do. The cause in 1.8.1 was a press that did not suppress the browser’s default handling; adding that one call is what fixes it

title: Clicking a file brings its card into view
highlights: Clicking a file now scrolls its card into view, not just its sheet. A sheet is twelve cells tall, so on a window shorter than the page the card could sit below the fold while its ring was drawn somewhere you could not see

The card is centred when it fits, aligned to its top when the window is shorter than the card, and the canvas is left alone when the card is already comfortably visible. This works the same whether the thumbnail strip is expanded or collapsed

Fixed a regression introduced in 1.8.1 and present in every version since: pressing a card’s text did not begin an edit unless the browser’s default press handling was suppressed explicitly. Adding `preventDefault` to the press is what makes a single click work
The click probe now also reports what happened after the press — whether a field appeared, and whether anything took the caret away

title: Typing no longer replaces the whole dish name
highlights: Fixed: clicking into a card’s text selected all of it, so the first character you typed replaced the entire name — type “!” into “Kung Pao Chicken” and you were left with “!”. That is why editing appeared not to work at all. The caret now goes to the end, and clicking within the text places it where you clicked
Added: the build number sits quietly beside the app name, so you can always tell which version is actually running

The app now asks for a newer version as soon as it opens, and again a few seconds later, instead of waiting for the browser’s next navigation. Updates should no longer need several reloads to take effect
Two new real-browser tests cover exactly this: typing into existing text must append, and the top bar must name the build

title: Re-run says what is actually wrong, and a way to report a dead click
highlights: Fixed: “Re-run all files” answered “Nothing to re-run — Add PDFs first” on a restored session, next to a list of files that had plainly been added. A saved session keeps the results, not the uploads, so the message now says the PDFs need adding again and why

Added: press Shift+? and then click, and the app reports which build is running, which element the browser actually delivered the press to, and how tall the text box is compared with the band it stands for. A click that lands on the photo instead of the text now says so outright
The Playwright suite covers re-run on a restored session, so that message cannot regress into the one it used to give

title: Clicking a card’s text now edits it — found in a real browser
highlights: Fixed: the bottom quarter of every card’s text band ignored clicks. The target-size rule forced every text box to 32px tall, but a header band at fit-to-width is about 24px — so the box overhung the photo below it, and the photo took those clicks
Fixed: card edits were lost on reload. The batch came back and the edits did not, because the card store read the saved snapshot before it had finished loading from disk

The Playwright suite now runs for real instead of reporting NOT RUN, and it is part of the gate: 12 tests against the production build cover clicking, the canvas not moving, the editor not shifting, reloads, undo and offline
Those tests caught both defects above. Neither was visible to the component tests, which have no layout and no hit-testing

title: A real browser in the loop, and one focus fix behind it
highlights: Added a Playwright suite that runs against the production build, covering the three things jsdom cannot see: whether a click actually lands on the text, whether the canvas moves when editing starts, and whether the edited text stays put when the formatting bar appears

Fixed: focus was taken in an effect, one frame after the field mounted. In that window the browser’s own press handling focused whatever sat under the pointer, so the caret landed wherever the mouse was rather than at the start of the text
The press now suppresses the browser’s default press behaviour and focus is taken in the same commit that mounts the field, so there is no unfocused frame
Escape now closes the editor from the text itself, because the formatting bar floats over the pane and can sit between the key and the field

title: One click on a card’s text now edits it
highlights: Fixed: the first click on a card’s text only selected the card, so editing took two clicks and the second one landed on something that had moved. Selecting a card reveals its band dividers, and those appeared under the pointer between press and release, swallowing the click
Text now begins editing on press rather than on release, so the gesture completes before anything can appear underneath it
The band dividers are drawn after the text boxes rather than between them, so they no longer paint over the last few pixels of a header or footer band

title: Your work survives a reload, and Clear all can be undone
highlights: Your session is saved: uploads, placements and every card edit are restored when you come back, so closing the tab is no longer a total loss
Clear all files now offers Undo. It used to be one click that destroyed the batch and every edit made to it, with no copy anywhere to recover from

Fixed: clicking into a card’s text moved the canvas. Focusing a text box scrolled the stack to reveal it, and the formatting bar appearing above the sheet shrank the canvas — both moved the page out from under the pointer
The text formatting bar now floats over the top of the sheet instead of taking 32px of canvas height the moment you start editing
Fixed: an unhandled render error white-screened the app and took every unsaved edit with it. A boundary now catches it and offers a reload
Removed the unused `batches` store from the database schema and the storage hook nothing called — a store that promised persistence the app did not have

title: Selecting a card no longer drags the page out from under the pointer
highlights: Fixed: clicking a card scrolled the canvas. Since clicking a card is also how you place a caret in its text or grab its photo, the paper moved mid-click and the caret or the drag was lost before it started
Selection and navigation are now separate: pressing a card selects it and nothing else. The canvas moves when you click a thumbnail or a file row, which are the two gestures that mean “take me there”

title: All the sheets at once, a strip that looks like the paper, and a rail you can search
highlights: Sheets are now one continuous column: every page of a 27-file batch is stacked in the canvas, 24px apart, and you scroll from the first to the last instead of paging through them

The sheet strip shows real miniatures — the dish photo at full fidelity, and each card’s text greeked into rules whose lengths follow the words, because a 6mm band at 64px is 3.7px tall and no font size survives that
Scrolling the canvas moves the active thumbnail, and clicking a thumbnail scrolls the canvas: one answer to which sheet you are on, whichever way you ask
Clicking the dark canvas beside the paper, or the white margin around its cells, clears the red selection and puts the right rail back to Sheet & print
Files gains a filter under Add PDFs for batches too long to scan, and each row shows where its first card landed (S2 · 07). Clicking a file scrolls to its card and selects it
The right rail can be collapsed from a button beside the Settings gear, giving its 260px back to the sheet
Top, Bottom and Text in the card inspector are a three-column grid with their labels stacked above the boxes, so a number is never squeezed between a label and its unit
Numeric fields are 28px tall rather than 24px: at 24 the digits sat on the border and the field read as a readout instead of something you can type into
Fixed: the sheet strip’s header could clip against the canvas on a long document

title: Sheet two gets its text and photos, and a cleared document comes back
highlights: Fixed: the second sheet showed empty cards — no text, no photo. Every page past the first twelve was seeded under its position in the page list instead of the cell it actually landed in, so the cards existed in the wrong place and the sheet looked blank

Fixed: after clearing the uploads and loading a PDF again, nothing came back — not even the first sheet. The seeding step remembered which cards it had already filled, and that memory outlived the cleared cards, so the second load filled nothing
The seeding step now asks the card store whether a card exists rather than trusting a cache, which is also what keeps it from overwriting a card you have edited

title: Every sheet is reachable, and a narrow window stops eating your work
highlights: Fixed: shrinking the window below 1024px used to unmount the workspace, and an unmount threw away your uploaded PDFs, photos and card edits. The workspace now stays mounted behind the notice, so widening the window brings everything back exactly as it was
The sheet opens fitted to the width of the window instead of the whole page, so every card is readable on load without zooming — the sheet scrolls vertically instead
Fit is a momentary action again: it returns the sheet to width-fit but never stays lit, because width-fit is already where the app rests

Sheet navigation: documents longer than twelve cards get a strip of sheet miniatures along the bottom of the canvas. Click one to jump to that sheet, or collapse it to a Sheets (2) pill to get the canvas height back
The canvas shows every sheet, not just the first — a thirteenth page used to exist in the export and nowhere on screen
Clicking a file in the Files rail jumps to the sheet its first card is on, and clicking a card on another sheet moves the canvas to it
Spacing and Margin fields are now sized like one half of a Size or Cell pair, so the number sits hard against its unit instead of floating at the far edge of an empty box
Numeric fields use tabular figures, so a unit never shifts sideways as the digits change

title: One unit for the whole sheet, and the dead print controls are gone
highlights: Units now offers millimetres, centimetres and inches, and the choice converts every field at once — the inspector, the sheet size, the cell size and the card boxes all read in the unit you picked
Nothing is stored in your chosen unit: dimensions stay millimetres in the document and in the exported PDF, so 21 cm and 210 mm are the same sheet and switching units cannot shift a value

Bleed, Trim marks and the Trim size dropdown have been removed. They never reached the file — the page was always the sheet's own size, and no trim mark was ever drawn — so they now stop promising one
The space between cards is called Spacing instead of Gutter
Number fields are 24px with no internal padding, so a number and its unit sit together instead of floating in an empty box; the inspector's rows and section padding are tightened to match
The header shows the app's real icon rather than a lettered red square
Text in a card's boxes is clipped to its own box with the exporter's own padding, so a short band can never bleed type into the photo or the next card
Fit is lit only while the sheet is actually fitted; any manual zoom clears it in the same gesture
The explanatory line under Print output is gone, along with the section it described

title: The photo gets the room the words do not need
highlights: Card text boxes now size themselves to their own text — a short dish name hands the surplus to the photo instead of leaving a blank band between the name and the picture, which grows from 63% to about 78% of the card
Text sits in the middle of its box instead of the top, so raising a box spreads the air on both sides of the words rather than opening one obvious gap beneath them
Settings opens on General: Units and Reduced motion first, then print output marked as global defaults for every sheet, with What's new still folded away at the bottom
Inspector numbers are visibly editable again — the field surface sits a step above the panel behind a real border that answers hover and focus, instead of blending in as static labels
Empty cell slots rest as a whisper on the paper and step up only under the pointer or keyboard focus, so an unfilled sheet no longer looks like a list of errors

title: The sheet opens fitted, and settings stops burying its own toggles
highlights: Fixed: the sheet came up at a literal 100% instead of filling the window — the canvas measurer attached to an element that did not exist yet and never looked again
The percentage is the real scale whether or not you chose it, and Fit is highlighted while the fit is live, so a computed 283% cannot be mistaken for one you set
Settings is centred over the sheet rather than appearing in the corner, and is a bounded panel instead of a full-height drawer
What's new is one collapsed row naming the current version, instead of eight releases above the fold — print output and reduced motion no longer need scrolling to reach
The sheet dimensions appear only in the inspector, where the sheet is; settings keeps trim, bleed, units and motion

title: One sheet, one bar, one inspector
highlights: The far-left navigation rail and the docked drawer under the sheet are gone: the A4 sheet now runs from the top bar to the bottom of the window
A single 48px bar holds the logo, − % + and Fit, the settings gear, and Export with a menu for every sheet as one PDF
The right rail is a contextual 260px inspector: a card's Top, Bottom and Text numbers when a card is selected, the sheet and print settings otherwise
Card heights are typed rather than dragged to: compact millimetre fields with arrow-key stepping, in place of the sliders' 6–55 mm sweep
One + Add PDFs button in the Files queue, with compact rows and hover-only retry actions; the duplicate header button, per-row size badges and the one-item tab strip are gone
One accent across selection, active borders, toggles and the primary button; no browser-blue sliders and no pure black
Settings opens as a dialog over the sheet instead of replacing the whole screen
Every explanatory paragraph under the controls is gone — the labels do the work

title: Zoom into the sheet, and shape a card by dragging it
highlights: The sheet zooms properly now: −, the percentage, +, and Fit in the toolbar, plus Ctrl/Cmd + wheel over the workspace
Fit is a mode — resizing the window keeps the sheet fitted until you step the zoom yourself, after which the pane scrolls
The floating slider and buttons over a photo are gone: double-click the frame to adjust, drag to pan, scroll to zoom, and Escape or a second double-click leaves with the framing kept
Scrolling while adjusting a photo zooms the photo and nothing else — the sheet no longer moves underneath it
Drag the boundary lines on a selected card to resize the text boxes directly, instead of reaching for the sliders
A text scale control makes a card's type bigger or smaller without touching the picture band: the layout re-wraps until it fits
Fixed a band clamp that could leave a 6 mm photo where 12 mm was promised — it affected any card given a large header

title: Format the words you select, not the whole box
highlights: Select some text and Bold, ink colour and highlight apply to just that stretch — the rest of the box keeps its own style
Red, green, amber and blue highlight boxes to match a reference card, plus an off switch
The formatting bar says whether it is about to change a selection or the whole box, so the two are never confused
Formatting survives typing: a highlighted word keeps its highlight when text is added, changed or deleted around it
Printed output matches: the export draws each stretch in its own weight, ink and highlight, verified against the PDF's own content stream
Picture controls were already complete — double-click to adjust, drag to pan, wheel or +/−/Reset to zoom — and now have tests covering each one
Panning no longer re-subscribes its listeners on every pointer move, which is what made dragging feel sticky

title: Photos stay in their cell, and the three zones stop overlapping
highlights: Cards are positioned from their own corner now — the preview was passing sheet coordinates into card-relative boxes, which shifted every zone down and right, pushing photos out of the cell and off the paper
The three zones stack with no overlap: header top, photo middle, footer bottom, tiling the card exactly
The card no longer obeys the 44 px control ladder. That ladder was a UI guideline, not geometry, and it was stretching a 10 mm header band to several times its real height
Text is typeset at the size the layout engine chose — it shrinks to fit a 52 mm wide band instead of growing past it, and lines are placed individually so the block can never outgrow its box
Every text and photo box has its own clipped, positioned container, so nothing can reach a neighbour

title: Twelve cards per sheet, and a README written for people who print things
highlights: Default sheet now holds twelve 52 x 67 mm cards — three across, four down — instead of nine larger ones
Each card starts at 10 / 42 / 15 mm, derived from the cell height rather than fixed, so a different card size still gets a sensible split
Reset in the band panel now returns to that per-card default instead of a hardcoded 13 / 20 tuned for the old 90 mm card
The export panel no longer claims pages are embedded as vectors — it says what actually happens: vector text, photos at their extracted resolution
README rewritten for the people using the app; build commands, architecture and release process moved to CONTRIBUTING.md

title: A deploy must reach a running client — now an engineering rule
highlights: §7 now requires all three parts of a working update path: a self-updating service worker, a controllerchange listener, and a visible reload affordance
The rule names the trap directly: a page keeps running the JavaScript it loaded at first paint, so an installed worker alone leaves the user on the old build
Auto-reload is allowed only where the app provably holds no unsaved state; otherwise the update is announced and the user chooses
The three conditions worth testing — not on first install, not during startup, once per worker — are written down with the code
§4.4 now notes that an installed PWA has no address bar, so the update notice is the only route to a new build

title: New versions now tell you they are ready
highlights: A deployed update used to take effect only after a manual refresh, because the page kept running the JavaScript it had already loaded
A “New version ready” notice now appears within a second or two of a new build taking over, with a Reload button
Reloading stays your choice: an automatic refresh would discard unsaved cards, which matters for a tab left open
The notice is not shown on a first install, and not while the page is still starting up

title: Fixed: cards arrived empty, and the band sliders were hidden
highlights: Fixed: a page was placed on the sheet but its card was seeded empty, so no photo and no text appeared — the lookup matched a document’s internal id against the file name the sheet uses
The top and bottom sliders now sit in a docked panel under the sheet, where nothing can clip or cover them
Selecting a card is enough to tune it; the sliders no longer have to be hunted for on the card itself
The panel draws the three-zone split and names the picture height, so the effect of a drag is visible as a number

title: Rebuilt around a three-zone card
highlights: Every cell is one card with three zones — top text, photo, bottom text — and each zone is edited in place
The Text tab and the sheet-wide Card Bands sliders are gone; a card carries its own top and bottom heights, tuned by selecting it
Upload now reads a page once and returns the dish photo, the name above it and the steps below it together
The header/instructions split follows where the photo actually sits on the page, so dish notes above a low photo stay with the name instead of becoming steps
Scanned pages with no text layer are read with OCR, so their cards are not blank; OCR loads only when needed and is never fetched for a normal PDF
Bold, ink colour and highlighter are per box, applied from a bar that appears under the card being edited
The exported PDF prints exactly the card: same bold, same colours, same highlights, same band heights, same photo framing
Fixed: photo placement is read from the PDF’s own transform matrices, which were being composed in the wrong order

title: Dish photos keep their shape, and can be moved and zoomed
highlights: Photos are no longer stretched: a dish keeps its own proportions however wide or tall the card is
Each photo sits in a defined picture box with a small inset, centred, leaving clear room for the text above and below
Anything zoomed past the box is clipped to it, so a picture can never sit on the text or cross a cut line
Double-click a photo to move and zoom it: drag to pan, scroll or pinch to zoom, or use the corner slider
Framing is kept per cell, so a dish stays where it was put — in the preview and in the printed sheet
Escape or Enter leaves the mode, and a reset button puts the photo back where it started

title: Step 1: every cell gets its dish photo
highlights: Each uploaded PDF places its own dish photo into its own cell
The embedded image is used when there is one, at full resolution and its own shape
When there is no embedded image — or the only one is the whole page — the page is rendered offscreen and the dish cropped out of the middle
A flattened card is recognised by its page-shaped image and cropped rather than shown whole
Fixed: the crop looked up the page in a cache the preview never filled, so it always came back empty
Oversized photos are scaled down, so a large scan cannot bloat the document

title: Three boxes on the card: type, photo, type
highlights: The exported card now holds the cropped dish photo only — the source page is never embedded, so its printed title and border box cannot come along
Fixed: image data arrives from the PDF worker after the page is read, so extraction was quietly failing and cards fell back to a page render
Page renders are gone from the card picture band entirely; a page with no photo says so instead of showing a screenshot
Header and footer stay live, editable text on the sheet and in the exported PDF
Layout, cell size and grid are unchanged

title: The dish photo is the photo, on every page
highlights: Fixed: the cell picture lookup could never find the extracted photo, so every card showed a full-page render instead
Fixed: photos and copy were read from page 1 only, so later pages of a multi-card PDF showed the first dish
Each card now takes its words and its photo from its own page, and never borrows another page’s dish
A page with no readable photo or copy leaves that band empty rather than showing another dish
Layout, cell size and grid are unchanged

title: The card fills itself, and the photo is the photo
highlights: A card arrives already written: the dish code, the dish name, and the plating steps are read off the page on upload
Steps come out as clean bullets, not a copy of the box they were printed in
The picture band shows the dish photo itself, pulled out of the PDF — not a re-render of the whole page
Click the words on any card to type into them; Escape or Enter puts them back
Colour and highlight for each card’s header and footer, on screen and in the exported PDF
Three across and three down: nine 64 × 90 mm cards on A4, 83% of the paper used
A page with no readable text leaves its card empty rather than inventing copy
Fixed: photo bytes handed back as a Uint8ClampedArray were rejected, so no photo ever appeared

title: The picture box holds picture, and the type is the right size
highlights: The picture band now shows the artwork only — the source page’s own printed text is cropped away
Text at both ends of a page: the artwork between them is kept, instead of the whole page
Header and footer are set at their real size and wrap where the printed card breaks
Fixed: card text was measured in points against a width in millimetres, so every word wrapped

title: A card with three bands, and one box to type in
highlights: Cards are header, picture, footer — the three bands always fill the card
Paste your copy once per page in the new Text tab; first line is the header, the rest is the footer
The picture fills its band completely and is clipped, so no white gaps
Move and zoom the picture inside its box; a framed picture can never reach the text
Header and footer heights are yours to set, in millimetres

title: Edit the sheet directly
highlights: Text on every cell is now editable in place — click a block and type
Move and zoom the page inside its cell; the text moves with it
Edits are per cell, so a page repeated twice can differ in each copy
The extra read-only preview pane is gone: the sheet is the workspace
Edited text is re-typeset in the exported PDF, still as vector, never a picture

title: See your pages in the cells
highlights: Every grid cell now shows the real page artwork, not just a filename
Artwork sits exactly where it will print, so the preview matches the export
Pages render once and are cached — switching sheets is instant
Pages that cannot render fall back to the filename instead of breaking
Returning to a sheet you already viewed shows its artwork straight away
Re-uploading a file with the same name shows the new pages, never the old ones

title: Print-ready sheet export
highlights: Export writes a real multi-page PDF — one output page per sheet
Source pages are embedded as vectors: text stays selectable, no rasterising
Cells are contain-fitted, so nothing is ever cropped
Cut guides are drawn on the gutter centrelines
Unreadable sources are skipped and reported, never faked

title: Fits the window
highlights: The app is exactly one viewport tall — no page scrolling
The sheet preview auto-scales to the space available, with a live zoom readout
Each pane owns its own scroll region

title: Multi-up sheet imposition
highlights: A4 sheet fits 12 cells at 52 x 67 mm with a 4 mm gutter for scissors
Cell size, gutter, margin, and sheet size are all adjustable, with a live cell count
Every page of every PDF becomes its own placeable object
Pages are contain-fitted into cells, so nothing is ever cropped
Cell numbers and cut guides show exactly where the sheet will be cut

title: Add PDFs actually imports
highlights: Add PDFs and Add more PDFs open a real file picker; drag and drop works too
Text blocks are extracted and grouped per page, with a first-page thumbnail
PDF reading runs in a lazily-loaded worker, so the app shell still loads fast
Unreadable, empty, and password-protected files fail with a clear reason
Renamed to CrewBTC

title: Desktop workspace shell
highlights: Three-pane workspace: batch queue, print canvas, inspector
Configurable trim, bleed, and crop-mark margins
Reduced-motion toggle that persists locally
Installable PWA with offline caching
